content.text: It destroyed thousands of London homes.
It destroyed St Paul’s Cathedral too.

visualText.notes:
Misconceptions
Pupils may think the whole of London was destroyed. Clarify that thousands of homes were destroyed, not every building in the city.

Background
The St Paul’s destroyed in the fire was the old medieval cathedral. The present St Paul’s was built later.

content.text: Winds carried flames between the houses.
Wooden houses were built close together.
The summer before the fire was dry.

reasons.line: The summer before the fire was dry.

reasons.notes:
Running
Talk through how each factor helped the fire spread. Ask pupils to explain the link between the factors and the flames.

Misconceptions
Pupils may think only one thing made the fire spread. Explain that wind carried flames, while close wooden houses and a dry summer helped the fire spread.

Background
Dry conditions can make materials catch fire more easily. Houses built close together leave flames a short distance to travel between buildings.

workedExample.notes:
Running
Pupils find each answer independently, then compare their working with a partner. Take feedback, asking how the first answer helps find the second.

Answers
1. 2½ m

Misconceptions
Pupils may multiply 10 by 3 before dividing, or stop at 2½ m after finding one quarter. Reinforce the order: divide by 4 to find one quarter, then multiply by 3 to find three quarters.
